channel.title: Event Handlers :: K-State CIS 400 Textbook
channel.description: In C#, we use event handlers (sometimes called event listeners in other languages) to register the behavior we want to happen in response to specific events. You’ve probably already used these, i.e. declaring a handler: private void OnEvent(object sender, EventArgs e) { // TODO: Respond to the event } Most event handlers follow the same pattern. They do not have a return value (their return type is void), and take two parameters. The first is always an object, and it is the source of the event (hence “sender”). The second is an EventArgs object, or a class descended from EventArgs, which provides details about the event.
